newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and West Bengal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu held "very positive and fruitful" discussion yesterday on water sharing and various other bilateral issues.
Former foreign minister A.S.M. Mustafizur Rahman, a close confidant of ex-prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, died of cancer at Dhaka's Combined Military Hospital on Saturday. He was 65. ---
West Bengal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu indicated that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina might go to India this weekend for Ganges water sharing accord.
The government has decided to revoke its order freezing government grant and increment for teachers of the institutions having "disastrous" SSC and HSC results.

West Bengal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu now visiting Bangladesh said that he would suggest the government of India to sign a short-term agreement with Bangladesh on the sharing of Ganges water. He said a permanent agreement on the sharing would be signed later on.
Government has decided to appoint more fertilizer dealers for 371 thanas having insufficient number of dealers to ensure adequate and timely supply of urea fertilizer to farmers at fair price.

The government has fixed the target to procure 0.15 million tonnes of rice and equal quantity of paddy during the current season to keep the market price of foodgrains stable and ensure fair price to the growers.
Economists and stock exchange experts have suggested a comprehensive reform programme to ensure positive performance of the share market as well as to protect the interest of the investors.
